stem.text: Write \( \int_{4}^{6} 2e^{x}\,dx \) as the limit of a right Riemann sum with n subintervals of equal width, using k as the index of summation.

worked_solution.text: The interval [4, 6] has length 2, so each of the n subintervals has width \( \Delta x = \frac{2}{n} \).
The right endpoint of the kth subinterval is \( x_k = 4 + \frac{2k}{n} \), for k = 1 to n.
Multiply the function value at each right endpoint by the width and take the limit: \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{k=1}^{n} 2e^{4 + \frac{2k}{n}} \cdot \frac{2}{n} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: definite integral as a limit of Riemann sums

options.label: \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{k=1}^{n} 2e^{\frac{2k}{n}} \cdot \frac{2}{n} \)
options.derivation: the sample points started at 0 instead of 4, so the sum is over [0, 2], an interval the integral never gives

options.label: \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{k=1}^{n} 2e^{4 + \frac{2k}{n}} \)
options.derivation: the function values at the right endpoints added with no subinterval width

options.label: \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{k=1}^{n} 2e^{4 + \frac{2k}{n}} \cdot \frac{1}{n} \)
options.derivation: the width taken as 1/n as though the interval had length 1, although the sample points step by 2/n
